newsitem.title: USA: PG&E sees 17c/shr gain from InterGen sale.
newsitem.headline: PG&E sees 17c/shr gain from InterGen sale.

text.p: Pacific Gas & Electric Co's PG&E Enterprises said Friday it will sell its interest in International Generating Co (InterGen) to Bechtel Enterprises for an expected after-tax gain of $70 million, or 17 cents a share.
The sale is expected to be completed before March 1997.
InterGen, a worldwide power generation company, was formed in early 1995 by the two organizations to develop, finance, own, and operate electric power plants outside the U.S. and Canada.

PG&E Enterprises manages PG&E's businesses other than gas transmission and California utility operations. Bechtel Enterprises is the development, financing, and ownership affiliate of Bechtel Group, Inc.

"While InterGen's primary strategy is to pursue power generation projects in many countries around the globe, PG&E has refined its international strategy to focus on a smaller set of countries where it will participate in multiple energy businesses with a focus on end-use energy customers," said Tony DiStefano, president of PG&E Enterprises.
PG&E Enterprises and Bechtel Enterprises will continue to own and manage U.S. Generating Company, a supplier of electric power in the United States since 1989.
USGen has ownership and management responsibilities for 17 electric power plants, accounting for nearly 3,400 megawatts of generating capacity.
